(a) Definitions.
Boathouse, as used in this article, a boathouse is an enclosed structure along the shoreline in which a boat is kept.
Dock, as used in this article, a dock means a wooden-decked structure, supported on piles and used to give passengers access to vessels.
(b) General. Any proposed land disturbance above the 360-foot contour line (normal water elevation) within 25 feet of said line may require a buffer variance. The determination as to whether or not a buffer variance will be required is to be made by the state department of natural resources, environmental protection division or it's designee. This includes the construction of docks, boat launching facilities and seawalls. (O.C.G.A. § 12-7-1, DNR/EPD Rules and Regulations 391-3-7.)
Persons who at the time of application thereof own property abutting 369-foot contour line of the Lake Tobesofkee Recreation Area and who hold current, valid, permits as described in section 17-54 and this section may construct a dock and/or boathouse at the 360-foot contour level upon the following conditions.
(c) Application.
(1) A person desiring to construct a dock or boathouse, either or both shall first make application to the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area on application forms provided by the same. In addition to the following, the applicant shall submit information prescribed by the Tobesofkee Recreation Area and the department of business development services.
a. A statement of the proposed location and length of a dock or boathouse as well as the height thereof which may not exceed the length and height hereinafter specified.
b. The plans and specifications by which the dock or boathouse, either or both are to be constructed shall be in such reasonable detail as may be prescribed by the department of business development services and shall be such as to make adequate provision for the safety of those using the dock or boathouse.
(2) Upon receipt of the application, plans and specifications by the Manager of Tobesofkee Recreation Area who shall forward same said documents to the Macon-Bibb County engineering Department; and they shall examine the same and visit the proposed site with the applicant. If they find that the application does not meet the location requirements or other requirements herein specified; they shall reject the same, stating in writing the reasons why it was rejected.
(3) Once the application is approved by the Macon-Bibb County engineering department, the applicant shall be forwarded to the business development services who shall examine the same together with the accompanying plans and specifications for compliance with applicable construction codes enforced in Macon-Bibb County. The department of business development services shall confer with the applicant if after the examination additional details or information is necessary to assure that the completed structure if built in accordance therewith will comply with such codes. Once the department approves the application, a construction permit shall be issued subject to fees as prescribed by the department of business development services and in accordance with the department's administrative procedures.
(d) Requirements.
(1) Any such dock or boathouse shall be located in front of the property or the person desiring to construct the same at a point which would place the entire structure between the sidelines of his or her property if such sidelines were extended to the nearest points on the 360-foot contour line and intersected with such contour line as nearly as possible at right angles.
(2) A dock or boathouse shall not be constructed where there is less than 100 feet of frontage at the 360-foot contour line. The shoreline will be measured from pin to pin.
(3) Docks or boathouses may have located thereon an enclosed area for recreational purposes, provided that it not exceed the maximum allotted boathouse dimensions. The total structure, including pilings, dock, boathouse and roof, shall extend no higher than 20 feet above the 360-foot contour line. Except for the installation of one water line to aid in the cleaning of fish and for similar purposes, there shall be no plumbing installed. Such area shall not be used for sleeping quarters or other human habitation, nor shall it contain bath or toilet facilities. No additional enclosed boathouses will be permitted. Open-sided boathouses will be permitted as long as they meet all other requirements and specification as set forth herein. Only one enclosed storage area may be located on open-sided boathouses.
(4) No dock shall be constructed any longer than is necessary to reach from the 360-foot contour line to a horizontal length of 40 feet, nor longer than is necessary to reach a ten-foot depth of water vertically, whichever is the shorter distance. As an additional limitation, no dock shall be constructed in such manner as to occupy in length or breadth more than 25 percent of the width of a slough or cove.
(5) Flotation docks and boathouses are not permitted.
(6) Whenever an existing dock or boathouse is to be replaced (or remodeled or repaired to an extent which exceeds in cost 50 percent of the value thereof), a new application shall be made in accordance with the procedures established in this section and such replacement, remodeling or reconstruction shall not occur until such time as all required approvals have been obtained. Existing boathouses may be repaired or replaced but not expanded. If an enclosed boathouse is torn down, destroyed or removed for any reason, any replacement shall be constructed in accordance with all current regulations and requirements of this section.
(7) If construction is not substantially commenced within six months after the final approval of an application, whether the same be for a new dock or boathouse, either or both, or for the repair, replacement or reconstruction of either or both, the permit shall expire, and the applicant shall not proceed until after having filed a new application and obtained approval thereof as provided in subsection (b).
(8) The annual permit required under section 17-54 and issued under the provisions of this section shall remain from its date as long as the dock and/or boathouse are properly constructed and maintained in a safe and presentable condition and for so long as the holder thereof is the owner of the property which enabled him to apply for the permit in the first instance. A permit issued under the provisions of this subsection will be transferred to a successor in title of such abutting land if there are no changes in the conditions which permitted the initial authorization and so long as the dock and/or boathouse are maintained in a presentable and safe condition.
(9) It shall be the responsibility of the owner to maintain docks and boathouses in a safe condition. All docks and boathouses are subject to periodic inspections by representatives of Tobesofkee Recreation Area. If a structure is found to be dilapidated or unsafe, the department of business development services shall be notified to inspect the same and to notify the responsible party of any repairs needed for continued use of the dock or boathouse. Failure to comply with such directions shall be grounds for revocation of the permit.
(10) Nevertheless it is a condition of the issuance of the permit that the holder thereof, or his or her successor in title, will nevertheless remove at his or her sole cost and expense any dock or boathouse and restore the area to its original condition upon 60 days written notice from the director of the department of business development services. This provision is made in view of the fact that the location of the dock and/or boathouse are upon public property and the owner of the abutting property acquires no vested right to continue to use and occupy such public property.
(11) Any person holding a permit for the construction, replacement, reconstruction or repair of a dock or boathouse shall be deemed to have a agreed to comply with all reasonable rules and regulations now or hereafter promulgated by Macon-Bibb County and the directions of the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area and the department of business development services with respect to the construction, maintenance or use of such dock or boathouse as well as with respect to the use of the lake or other areas of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area.
(12) No recreation area constructed in connection with a dock or boathouse shall at any time be used for human habitation. Recreational uses which generate noise, odors or other practices which constitute a nuisance shall be grounds for revocation of the permit herein granted and for ordering the owner to remove the facility.
(13) Reserved.
(14) The terms "owner," "responsible party," "applicant," "holder of the permit" and similar words and phrases shall be construed to mean the person owning private property abutting the 369-foot contour line and the Tobesofkee Recreation Area, and are not intended to import any ownership by anyone of the area between the 360- and 369-foot contour lines. "Owner" also designated the person for compliance with the provisions of this section.
(15) Any person aggrieved by action of the Manager, Tobesofkee Recreation Area, or the department of business development services under the provisions of this section may appeal in writing to the commission within 30 days after receipt of such written notice of a decision of either official and the commission shall hold a hearing upon the appeal at which the appellant shall be entitled to be present and present evidence to support the appeal. The decision of the commission on the appeal shall be final.
(16) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this section, and notwithstanding any limitation in the building code of Macon-Bibb County, the department of business development services is constituted as the agency for the enforcement of the Tobesofkee regulations to the extent that they relate to electrical installations to and from docks and boathouses and as they relate to regulations respecting the potable water systems for docks and boathouses. The director of the department of business development services, or his or her designee, is hereby vested with full authority and power to enforce the provisions of the building code including the power to issue summonses or citations for violations of such codes. The director, or his or her designee, is hereby authorized to administer the provisions of the building code, to make inspections and to take such action as necessary, proper and convenient to cause violators of the code to be punished.
(e) Specific requirements for docks or boathouses.
(1) Only one boat dock or boathouse is permitted on each lot. Permanent structures shall be a minimum of 15 feet from side property lines.
(2) Boat docks or boathouses shall extend no further than 40 feet from the 360-foot contour line. A shorter length may be required where a narrow cove is involved or if the dock would extend in front of an adjacent lot. Under no circumstances will a dock be permitted where access of adjacent property owners would be limited. Overall concerns for safety shall dictate the location and length of docks which will be approved by the Lake Tobesofkee Manager or his or her designated agent.
(3) Docks shall be stationary. (No floating docks will be permitted.)
(4) Docks or boathouses shall comply with the following:
a. Maximum of six-foot wide cat walk.
b. Maximum platform size shall be 12 feet by 20 feet.
c. If a dock (walkway) and boathouse are constructed as a single unit the width shall be no greater than 30 feet.
d. Maximum interior dimension of the boathouse shall be 24 feet by 26 feet.
e. Maximum extension into the lake is 40 feet.
f. Maximum roof height is 20 feet above the 360-foot contour line (normal elevation).
g. Minimum size of water line is one-inch and must be used only for cleaning fish.
h. No sanitary plumbing is permitted, nor can recreation area be used for sleeping purposes or human habitation.
(5) Boat lifts attached to docks must be approved prior to installation. A maximum of two full-sized boat lifts will be allowed per dock as long as the overall length is within the required guidelines and is approved by the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area or his or her designee. The boat lift cannot be placed closer than 15 feet from the adjoining property line. Each full-sized lift may have a matching canopy frame. The frame must be dome-shaped. No pitch frame canopy will be allowed. The color and type of material must be approved by the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area or his or her designee prior to installation. Natural colors are recommended (dark blue or dark green).
(6) Personal watercraft (PWC) ramps must be approved prior to installation. A maximum of two PWC ramps may be attached to a dock or boathouse as long as the overall length is within the required guidelines and is approved by the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area or his or her designee. The PWC ramp may be constructed of wood or high-density polyethylene and must be maintained in a safe and presentable condition.
(f) Requirements for seawalls. Persons who at the time of application thereof own property abutting the 369-foot contour line of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area and who hold current, valid permits as described in section 17-54 may construct a seawall at the 360-foot contour level upon the following conditions: The construction of a new seawall may require a buffer variance permit from the department of natural resources, environmental protection division.
(1) A person desiring to construct a seawall shall first make application to the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area. In addition to the following, the applicant shall submit information prescribed by the Tobesofkee Recreation Area and the department of business development services.
(2) Seawall construction will require proper erosion and sedimentation controls. After completion of the seawall and until the vegetative buffer is restored, a silt fence must be installed and maintained just behind the new seawall at ground level.
(3) Seawall construction plans should show the following:
a. The length of shoreline to be fronted by the seawall.
b. The type of foundation to be installed and depth below ground level.
c. The type of materials to be used for construction of the seawall.
d. The height of the seawall should be no higher than necessary to stabilize shoreline.
(4) The distance between the proposed seawall and the existing shoreline shall not exceed two feet.
(5) The location of the proposed seawall must be staked at 25-foot intervals in order for inspectors to assure the original contour is adhered to as close as possible. For very irregular shoreline, stakes shall be no more than ten feet apart.
(6) Creosote timbers are prohibited for new seawall construction.
Any variance from the requirements as set forth in this section must be approved by the commission.
1966:
Where there are subdivisions or apartment properties whose boundaries abut the 369-foot contour line at Lake Tobesofkee, the property owners' association of the subdivision or the apartment owner or a tenants' association may make application to the commission for approval to construct boat launching facilities and/or community boat docks. In determining whether a permit will be granted, the commission shall be authorized to take into account all relevant facts affecting the lake, the revenues derived therefrom, impact on other property owners, as well as other relevant considerations. If approved, board launching facilities and/or community boat docks may be established under the following conditions:
(1) The applicant shall be fully responsible for the maintenance of the boat-launching facilities and/or community boat docks and preservation of safety and cleanliness.
(2) The applicant agrees to abide by all rules and regulations as set forth by this Code and the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area.
(3) Upon failure of the applicant or successor to maintain the facility or boat dock in a clean, safe and aesthetically satisfactory condition, the permit may be revoked by Macon-Bibb County.
(4) In determining whether to issue a permit, the governing authority may take into consideration this entire article, and particularly subsection 17-55(d)(10).
(5) Approval of such a facility and/or boat dock and its subsequent operation by the applicant or a successor to the applicant shall entitle the residents of the subdivision or apartment complex to use the lake for swimming, fishing, boating or skiing purposes but only if such users hold a current valid annual permit as described in subsection 17-54(b).
1967:
(a) Persons owning property abutting the 369-foot contour line around Lake Tobesofkee are hereby authorized to use so much of the Tobesofkee Park property as lies between the 369-foot contour line and the 360-foot contour line and between the sidelines of the property of such persons which would exist if the property line began at the present terminus of such property lines at the 369-foot contour line and extended to the 360-foot contour line so that such extended side property lines would intersect with the 360-foot contour line at the nearest point so that such extended sideline will be the shortest distance between the 369-foot contour line and 360-foot contour line. If, by reason of physical circumstances such as land contours, the application of the foregoing rule would deny a person owning property abutting the 369-foot contour line reasonable access to the 360-foot contour line, or would otherwise produce a manifest absurdity, the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area is authorized, with due consideration to the effects on adjoining property owners, to specify how the sidelines of the property of such owner will be extended so as to afford some access to the 360-foot contour line. However, in order to construct a dock or boathouse there must be a minimum width of 100 feet of water frontage at the 360-foot contour line.
(b) The use and occupancy which may be made by abutting property owners shall be in common with that of the general public and shall be such as is afforded to the public with respect to other Macon-Bibb County property and rights-of-way.
(c) Notwithstanding, Macon-Bibb County reserves the full and complete right to flood at will such area, and to install therein public utilities, including, but not limited to, water and sewer lines and to maintain the same or to permit the Macon-Bibb County water and sewerage authority to do so. Macon-Bibb County further reserves full right to make such use of the area as it shall deem necessary or convenient in the maintenance of the lake itself.
(d) Macon-Bibb County shall have no liability to property owners or third parties by any use made of the above-described area by owners of abutting property.
(e) Nothing in this section shall be construed as granting any right to cut trees, dig ditches, channels or otherwise make cuts, fill, excavate or otherwise alter the natural elevation or to erect and maintain fences in the area below the 369-foot contour line, but on the contrary, all of such activities are specifically prohibited except with the specific approval of Macon-Bibb County after written application therefor giving adequate justification; provided, however, that nothing in this section shall be deemed to require the removal of any fences which were in existence and which were used for the enclosure of cattle at the time the Tobesofkee Recreation Area was acquired by Bibb County; and, provided further, that if at any time the land formerly used for the grazing of cattle has changed in its use, then and at that time, the fences shall be removed and shall not thereafter be maintained.
(f) Tree removal.
(1) To protect the vegetative buffer surrounding the lake, the removal of any trees with a diameter of more than three inches is prohibited without prior written approval of the commission.
(2) Native ornamental trees such as dogwoods, magnolias, flowering fruit trees, etc. of any size, may not be removed without prior written approval of the commission.
(3) Tree removal requests must include a tree survey performed by a registered forester, professional landscape architect or arborist, which shows all trees in the proposed area, the specific trees to be removed, the total number of trees to be removed, the value of the trees to be removed and the process by which they will be removed.
(4) If tree removal involves significant earth disturbance, proper erosion and sedimentation controls must be followed, including installing a silt fence to protect the shoreline and re-vegetative plan.
(5) All portions of the tree/s (limbs, stumps, etc.) must be properly removed from the lot. Dumping, burying, or otherwise disposing of any portion of the tree on Macon-Bibb County property, lease lots, or lake is prohibited.
(g) Dredging.
(1) Dredging will be permitted up to 500 cubic yards per lot. Greater amounts will require approval from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and additional agencies.
(2) Dredging plans must be submitted and approved before work begins. A dredging permit must be obtained prior to any dredging activity.
(3) By obtaining a dredging permit from Macon-Bibb County the permittee agrees to:
a. Abide by all governmental rules, laws, regulations, directives and statutes.
b. Acquire all necessary governmental permits or licenses, which may include, but shall not be limited to, a soil distributing activity permit.
(4) Applicants must provide the volume of material to be removed. A qualified engineer or surveyor should determine this information (especially for large projects over 100 cubic yards). An estimate sheet is to be attached to the permit request.
(5) Removal of original lake bottom is prohibited. The sole purpose for dredging is to remove silt or sedimentation that has accumulated over time.
(6) The material removed from the lake shall be disposed of in upland area so as to avoid re-entry into the lake.
(h) Macon-Bibb County grants only such use of the area described in this section as it may lawfully grant.
1968: No person shall have or acquire any rights in land or any vested interest to the continuance of any access permit or a permit for the construction and maintenance of a dock or boathouse nor to the continuance of these regulations in their present form. This provision is necessary for the protection of the public property and all permits for any such purposes are expressly made subject to this section.
1969: In addition to such other powers and authority as they may have, the superintendent of the Lake Tobesofkee Recreation Area, the rangers and other members of the staff (including, but not limited to, lifeguards) are hereby expressly authorized and empowered to issue citations to person violating any of the rules and regulations of the Lake Tobesofkee Recreation Area contained in this Code. Immediately after issuing the citation, the person issuing the same shall forward a copy to the appropriate prosecuting official of Macon-Bibb County for appropriate further action. Municipal court, state court, and magistrate court shall have concurrent jurisdiction over violations of this article.
1970:
(a) The rules and regulations applicable to the Lake Tobesofkee Recreation Area, exclusive of those promulgated by the Director of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area, are as follows:
General.
(1) The cardinal rule of conduct for all persons utilizing the Lake Tobesofkee Recreation Area ("the area") is that of common courtesy and respect for the rights of others. Most problems can be avoided if this rule is recognized.
(2) No person may be admitted to or use the facilities of Lake Tobesofkee without payment of the appropriate fee. Evidence of fee payment shall be retained by every person admitted on a daily basis and shall be produced upon request of area personnel or other authorized individual.
(3) All persons using the Tobesofkee Recreation Area are expected to comply with all of the laws of the state regulating parks, recreation areas, camping, boating, skiing and fishing, as well as with the applicable rules of the state department of natural resources and of Macon-Bibb County.
(4) All children under 14 years of age must be supervised by an adult while in or upon any body of water within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area.
(5) Hunting, trapping or otherwise pursuing or catching any wildlife within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area is strictly prohibited.
(6) Persons having boats in the water at the marina and at the apartment complexes on the lake must possess a current valid annual permit. All boats entering the marina for the purpose of boating will be required to purchase tickets at a gate house prior to entry, or must be the holder of a current annual permit.
(7) All children under 16 years of age must wear a helmet when riding a bicycle anywhere inside parks.
(8) Claystone and Arrowhead Parks open at 6:00 a.m. and close at 9:30 p.m. throughout the year. Sandy Beach Park hours vary from time to time according to the season. Area office hours are from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Sandy Beach Waterpark shall operate 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Monday through Sunday during the water park season which shall be from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend.
(9) Off-road vehicles (ATVs, dirt bikes, go carts, motorized scooters, etc.) are prohibited. Golf carts are likewise prohibited with the exception of those utilized by disabled individuals and displaying a valid handicap sticker.
(10) The possession or consumption of alcoholic beverages within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area is prohibited, except under special circumstances approved by the commission and within areas designated by the Manager.
(11) Discharge of any firearm within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area shall be unlawful, unless express written permission for such has been authorized by the commission.
(12) Possession of any explosive substance, including fireworks, within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area shall be unlawful unless express written permission for such has been authorized by the commission.
(13) Motorized vehicles may be operated only upon designated roadways and shall be parked only in officially designated areas.
(14) No person shall drive any motor vehicle of any character on the roadways of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area at a speed greater than 15 miles per hour.
(15) Pets are not permitted within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area unless on a leash. Under no circumstances are pets permitted on beach areas.
(16) The Macon-Bibb County boat ramp docks are to be used only for assistance in launching or removing boats from the water. Use of the boat ramp dock for sunbathing and the placing thereon of lawn chairs and other equipment are prohibited.
(17) No person, firm or corporation shall deposit within the Tobesofkee Recreation Area in any of the parks below the 369-foot contour line any dirt, rock, debris or waste matter whether it is solid waste matter, garbage, human waste or other material, which might contaminate the ground or the lake. All waste matter shall be disposed of in approved facilities.
(18) Every person shall at all times obey and comply with directions given by all official regulatory signs posted within the area.
(19) Utilization of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area and its facilities is at the risk of the user. Macon-Bibb County assumes no responsibility for injury to persons or property arising from the utilization of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area.
(20) Persons wishing to utilize a picnic shelter may reserve a shelter in advance by contacting the area office and paying a reservation fee. Shelters not reserved in advance are available on a first come, first serve basis. Payment of a shelter reservation fee does not entitle anyone to enter the park free of charge. Each person desiring to enter the park shall pay the regular admission fee.
Camping.
(21) Campsites may be reserved by contacting the area office.
(22) Camping in areas other than designated camping areas is prohibited unless express, written authorization of the Manager is obtained.
(23) Payment of camping fees entitles the authorized persons to make use of campsites, beaches, and other facilities not requiring any other additional fees. Payment of camping fees covers admission to other site parks in addition to the one in which the paying parties are camping.
(24) Persons desiring to camp must pay camping fees in advance and obtain a permit from the gate stations; however, campers entering after 10:00 p.m. and prior to 6:00 a.m. may camp for the night, provided camping and other fees are paid not later than 9:00 a.m. on the morning immediately following entry.
(25) Check out time for camping is 12:00 noon. Campers remaining after 12:00 noon on any day will be charged for an additional day's camping.
(26) Camping is limited to 14 consecutive nights at any one site. After 14 consecutive nights, campers and the unit (RV, camper, trailer, etc.) must move to another site designated by the Manager (Waterfront sites in Arrowhead Park and the pull-through sites in Claystone Park are not included). Campers may stay a total of seven nights within a 30-night period at the waterfront sites in Arrowhead Park and pull-through sites at Claystone Park. After a total of seven nights during any 30-night period, campers and the unit (RV, camper, trailer, etc.) must vacate these sites for 30 consecutive nights before re-occupying any one of these sites.
(27) Campers who bring boats must pay the daily boat fee regardless of whether the boat is in the water or at a designated parking area. Boats and boat trailers shall not be parked at the campsites.
(28) Visitors to any occupied campsite must pay the general admission fee required of all persons. Issuance of a camping permit does not entitle visitors to enter the park area free of charge.
(29) Tent camping is permitted in RV sites. Camping occupancy is limited to one camping unit; (RV, pop-up, trailer or family tent) and one additional small tent per campsite. Each campsite is permitted two additional vehicles. Tent camping is not permitted in pull-through and sewer access sites.
(30) The use of major electrical appliances such as, but not limited to, refrigerators, washing machines, ice makers, and so forth is not permitted outside any camping unit (RV, pop-up, trailer, or tent).
(31) Camp fires are permitted only in designated areas and only when supervised by adults.
(32) Persons desiring to arrange for group camping should consult the area office in advance of applicable rules.
(33) Loud, boisterous conduct, including playing radios or other sound-producing devices at loud levels, is prohibited. Disorderly conduct, drunkenness, or obscene language is prohibited.
(34) Oversized vehicles such as tractor trailer trucks, automotive wreckers, etc., shall not be parked at camp sites. This prohibition does not apply to motor homes used for camping.
(35) Persons registering to camp must be 21 years of age or older.
(36) After 9:00 p.m. all children under 16 years of age must be accompanied by an adult unless they are at their campsite. Parents shall be responsible for the actions of their children.
(37) Pets are allowed in the campground if kept on a leash and attended at all times. Unleashed pets and those whose behavior disturbs other campers must be removed from the park by the owner. Under no circumstances are pets permitted on beach areas.
Fishing, boating and skiing.
(38) Except as provided in subsection (43), fishing, boating and skiing are authorized only for those people who hold a current day's ticket or a current annual permit in their possession.
(39) Fishermen, boaters, and skiers are cautioned to comply with all state and local regulations respecting those activities.
(40) Persons desiring to night fish after park hours must purchase tickets before park gates close, or have a current annual permit.
(41) Fishing is prohibited in swimming areas when the lake is open to swimmers.
(42) Fishing from public boat docks when boats are present is prohibited.
(43) Skiers and operators of boats towing skiers must exercise due care for the safety and welfare of others. Skiing in lake coves is specifically prohibited.
(44) Persons 65 years of age or older may fish without payment of an admission fee, provided they have obtained a senior citizen's pass at the area office.
(45) For the present, no limitation is placed upon the horsepower of motors. However, Macon-Bibb County reserves the right to place limits on the size of motorboat motors should the commission determine that to be in the public interest.
(46) All fishermen must carry licenses, as required by the state.
(47) No trout lines, set hooks, baskets, nets, jugs, or any type of commercial fishing gear shall be permitted. Cast nets and landing nets may be used in compliance with state laws.
(48) Fishing from bridges, right-of-way of roads and boat ramp docks is prohibited.
(49) No vessel, including sail boards, shall be permitted to enter any swimming area or any area designated as a no boat area.
Swimming.
(50) Swimming at all park sites must be confined to areas designated for that purpose.
(51) Diving or jumping from public docks and bridges is prohibited.
(52) Swimming is permitted during daylight hours only. Persons choosing to swim when lifeguards are not on duty do so at their own risk.
(53) Scuba diving in Lake Tobesofkee is prohibited unless the express written permission of the Manager is obtained.
(b) Official copies of these rules and regulations, and those promulgated by the Director of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area, are to be maintained in the office of the Clerk of Commission and the office of the Manager of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area.
(c) If any provision of this section or any rule or regulation promulgated by the Director of the Tobesofkee Recreation Area is in genuine conflict with any state or federal law or requirement, the conflict shall be resolved in accordance with law.
(Ord. of 6-20-2017(2); Ord. of 7-19-2022, § 3; Ord. No. O-22-0035, § 3, 7-19-2022)

The policy of equal opportunity applies to every aspect of County employment, policy and practice.

1974:
As used in this Article, the following terms have the following meanings:
(1) "Applicant" means any person considered or who requests to be considered for employment by Macon-Bibb County.
(2) "County agency" means any office, department, agency, board or commission of Macon-Bibb County.
(3) "Employee" means all persons engaged in the operation or conduct of any business, whether as owner, any member of owner's family, partner, associate, agent, manager, or representative, and any and all other persons engaged or employed in said business.
(4) "Employment" means any occupation, vocation, job, work for pay or employment, including temporary or seasonal work, contracted work, contingent work and work through the services of a temporary or other employment agency. "Employment" shall not, for the purposes of this chapter, include membership in any law enforcement agency.
(5) "Conviction" means any sentence arising from a verdict or plea of guilty or nolo contendere, including a sentence of incarceration, a suspended sentence, a sentence of probation or a sentence of unconditional discharge.
(6) "Inquiry" means any direct or indirect conduct intended to gather information, using any mode of communication.
(7) "Interview" means any direct contact by the employer with the applicant, whether in person or by telephone, to discuss the employment being sought or the applicant's qualifications.

1975:

1993:
(a) Duration, course of training. After selection for employment with the fire department, the person shall then undergo prescribed training. The course of training shall be determined and approved by the chief.
(b) Unsatisfactory performance by trainee. Any trainee whose performance is unsatisfactory during the aforesaid training period shall be brought before the chief and after explanation of the deficiency in question by the training officer, the chief shall determine whether the trainee shall be retained in the training program or dismissed.
(c) Assignment to duty. Upon satisfactory completion of the required training program, trainees shall be sworn to faithfully perform their duties by the chief and shall be assigned to duty on a probationary status.
(d) Duration of probationary status. After the completion of three hundred sixty-five (365) days of satisfactory probationary service, probationary employees shall be eligible to be promoted to nonprobationary status by official action of the mayor, as classified career employees of their respective departments; provided, however, that the chief may, with the approval of the mayor, extent the probationary service of an employee for a period not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days if such action is deemed to be in the best interest of Macon-Bibb County and the employee.
1994:
(a) Anniversary performance evaluation. All classified career employees of the fire departments shall be rated on performance no less than once each year on the anniversary date of employment.
(b) Performance rating forms. The performance rating forms used shall be those approved by the chief and the director, department of human resources.
(c) Trainees. Trainees shall be given a written performance evaluation report by the department training officer at the end of their initial training period. This report shall be signed by the trainee and made a part of his personnel records.
(d) Probationary employees. Probationary employees shall be given a written performance evaluation at the end of three (3), six (6) and nine (9) months. Following satisfactory completion of their probationary period they shall be given a full year's performance evaluation on their anniversary date.
(e) Nonprobationary employees. Nonprobationary employees shall receive a yearly performance evaluation on their anniversary date.
(f) Rating by immediate supervisor. Each person shall be rated by his immediate supervisor in the chain of command, and shall be endorsed by the next three (3) supervisors in the chain of command. A failure of any endorsing supervisor to agree with the evaluating supervisor's evaluation shall automatically place the performance evaluation in an appeal status.
(g) Evaluator. Each evaluator shall be a minimum of one rank higher than the person rated and each endorser shall be at least one rank higher than the first and subsequent endorser.
(h) Transferred employees. Employees transferred from one (1) supervisor to another shall be rated by the releasing supervisor on an interim rating form approved by the chief when the releasing supervisor has supervised the employee thirty (30) or more work days. This evaluation shall be signed by the employee and made available to the new supervisor.
(i) Criteria for promotion. To be eligible to stand for any promotion examination or to qualify for promotion from a promotion register, an employee must have been rated as competent or better on his or her last annual performance evaluation, with the preceding annual performance evaluation rated at no less than satisfactory.
1995:
(a) No appeal shall be permitted when the evaluator and subsequent endorsers agree on the evaluation.
(b) If one (1) endorser out of three (3) disagrees with the evaluator's evaluation, the employee's evaluation shall automatically be appealed to an evaluation appeal committee.
(c) The evaluation appeal committee shall be made up of a nonvoting presiding officer, who shall be the director, department of personnel or a designee of the director, and two senior officers, two (2) sergeants, and one (1) private, none of whom have been directly associated with the appealing officer. The voting members of the committee shall be appointed by the mayor or county manager.
(d) The evaluation appeal committee has the right to request appearances of other employees who have knowledge of the appealing employee's performance. The decision of the committee shall be forwarded to the chief for review and concurrence or nonconcurrence.
(e) In the event of nonconcurrence with a recommended evaluation change the original evaluation shall be retained. There shall be no appeal of the chief's decision.

1998:
(a) Physical examination. The chief of the fire department or the mayor may require any member of the department rated as a classified career employee to take a thorough physical examination if deemed necessary. Such examination shall be conducted by a physician selected by the mayor for conducting the examination and the cost shall be borne by Macon-Bibb County. The employee required to take such physical examination shall present a certificate from the examining physician stating whether or not the employee is physically able to fulfill the duties of his position with the department. If the employee is ruled physically unable to perform his duties, the following actions may be taken as appropriate:
(1) Placement on accrued sick leave pending clearance by a physician to return to work;
(2) Retirement under the disability retirement feature of the pension plan upon committee approval;
(3) Early retirement; or
(4) Termination.
(b) Program of study. All levels of supervisors in the fire department shall maintain a program of study in fire department management and operational fields in accordance with the minimum recommended standards established by resolution of the commission.
(c) Physical fitness standards.
(1) Applicants for employment in the fire department must meet the established minimum physical standards for the job classification for which they apply. As a condition of continued employment, all classified career employees in the fire department must meet the established minimum physical standards for their particular classification.
(2) The fire chief, in conjunction with a physician, shall have the authority to formulate and establish the appropriate minimum physical standards for each particular job description within the department. Such standards shall bear a reasonable relationship to the requirements of the particular job.
(3) The minimum standards of fitness shall be applied equally to all applicants or employees within a particular job description.
(4) Physical fitness training program.
a. If a classified career employee of the fire department fails to pass the minimum fitness standard for his particular job description, he or she shall be given an opportunity to participate in a physical fitness program for the purpose of meeting the minimum physical fitness standard for his or her job qualification. If such an employee does not meet the minimum physical fitness standard within a prescribed time limit, the chief shall take appropriate disciplinary action unless such employee is unable to meet such standards because of a medical condition verified to exist and being of a correctable temporary nature.
b. It shall be the responsibility of a physician and a physical conditioning specialist to suggest the appropriate physical fitness training program for the employee. The chief in conjunction with a physician and a physical conditioning specialist shall determine the length of time, not to exceed one-year, within which the employee must bring himself up to the applicable minimum physical standards.
c. At all times, it shall be within the authority of the chief to take necessary and reasonable disciplinary measures to ensure that the physical fitness standard is met and maintained.
1999:
Service requirements indicated for positions below shall be required before any member of the fire department is eligible for promotion to such position:
(1) A minimum of twelve (12) years' service with a recognized paid fire department shall be required before any person shall be eligible to be appointed chief or assistant chief of the fire department. A bachelor's degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute two (2) years' experience. An associate degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute one (1) years' experience.
(2) Firefighters above the rank of sergeant with a minimum of ten (10) years' service in the Macon-Bibb County fire department are eligible for appointment to the positions of battalion chief, training director or fire prevention director. A bachelor's degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute two (2) years' experience. An associate degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute one (1) years' experience.
(3) Lieutenants with a minimum of ten (10) years' service with the Macon-Bibb County fire department who have served at least one (1) year as lieutenant shall be eligible for promotion to captain. A bachelor's degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute two (2) years' experience. An associate degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute one (1) years' experience.
(4) Sergeants with a minimum of eight (8) years' service with the Macon-Bibb County fire department who have served at least one (1) year as sergeant shall be eligible for promotion to the position of lieutenant. A bachelor's degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute two (2) years' experience. An associate degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute one (1) years' experience.
(5) Privates with a minimum of six (6) years' non-probationary service with the Macon-Bibb County fire department and minimum of two (2) years of emergency apparatus driving experience with the department shall be eligible for promotion to the position of sergeant. A bachelor's degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute two (2) years' experience. An associate degree in fire sciences, chemistry or a related field shall constitute one (1) years experience.
(Ord. No. O-14-0036, § 3, 6-17-2014)

2009:
(a) There is hereby created and established the Macon-Bibb County Fire Civil Service Board which shall consist of five members who shall have been residents of Macon-Bibb County for two years or more. The members of the Macon-Bibb County Civil Service Board shall be appointed by the Mayor and approved by the Commission and shall serve a four year term. The members shall annually elect one of their members as chairman of the board and one member as vice-chairman. Three members of the board shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business. Vacancies in the office of said board created by death, resignation, or otherwise shall be filled for the unexpired term by an appointment of the Mayor with the approval of the Commission. No member of the board shall be a current employee of Macon-Bibb County. Members of the board shall be limited to two consecutive full terms of office on the board. Filling more than one-half of an unexpired term of office shall constitute a full term of office.

(c) The members of the board shall serve without compensation, except that the Commission may authorize payment to members on a per diem basis for the time actually devoted to the business of the board.
(d) The board shall keep its office and shall hold its meetings in the Macon-Bibb County Human Resources Department, and all of said meetings shall be open to the public. The interview shall consist of personal meeting with the candidates to evaluate their training, experience, and personal qualifications. If it is determined by the board that a candidate's qualifications match the requirements of the Position, the board shall designate the candidate as qualified for the Position. The candidate shall then be eligible for consideration by the appointing authority in accordance with Sec. 18-79 of this Chapter.

(3) To keep minutes of its own meeting and such other records as the board may deem necessary.
(4) To examine and approve or modify the annual report prepared by the secretary and submit such report to the Commission on or before July 1 of each year transmitting therewith any suggestions it may approve for the more effectual accomplishment of the purpose of this fire civil service system; and to supervise generally the work of the secretary in the administration of the provisions of this system.

2017: It is the purpose of this article to describe a comprehensive system of reporting incidents, accidents and other occurrences which involve or may involve Macon-Bibb County employees or vehicles, either or both, or which may be observed by Macon-Bibb County employees in the course of their employment.
2018:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Accident means an undesired event that results in physical harm to a person or damage to property whether or not the event is a "pure accident," or is attributable to negligence on the part of one or more persons.
Incident means an event which occurs or is observed by Macon-Bibb County personnel while engaged on Macon-Bibb County business and which is one which is unexpected and is outside the normal course of events, and in the happening of which Macon-Bibb County has or may reasonably be expected to have more than a casual interest.
Occurrence means an all-encompassing term which includes any event, whether or not resulting in known damage or a known personal injury, whether or not involving motor vehicles belonging to Macon-Bibb County and whether or not resulting in known damage to Macon-Bibb County property or personal injury to Macon-Bibb County employees or others, but involves Macon-Bibb County personnel or property, or an activity in which Macon-Bibb County has or may have an interest.
2019:
(a) Whenever an accident, incident or occurrence is observed by one or more Macon-Bibb County employees, the same shall be reported in writing as hereinafter provided.
(b) If the accident, incident or occurrence is observed by only one Macon-Bibb County employee, it shall be the duty of that employee to make the required report. If the same be observed by more than one Macon-Bibb County employee, it shall be the duty of the senior Macon-Bibb County employee present and physically able to do so, to make the required report.
(c) Reports shall be completed and filed as herein prescribed as soon as possible, but in any event within 24 hours.
2020:

2021:

2022: It shall be the duty of any person charged with filing reports to see that the same are completely filled out, and that the information required is accurate in every detail and is legible.
2023:
(a) It shall be the duty of each department head to insure that all employees of that department become familiar with the reporting mandates, the place of filing reports, and the other requirements of this article.

2028:

2029: Whenever any claim is made or proceeding is brought against any employee, either against him asserting personal liability for damages arising out of the performance of his duties or in any way connected therewith, whether based on negligence, violation of contract rights or violation of civil, constitutional, common law or other statutory rights, whether federal, state or local, Macon-Bibb County shall, upon his written request, provide for his defense by an attorney selected by Macon-Bibb County unless otherwise limited by the terms of this article. Macon-Bibb County may decline defense of an employee or decline payment of a claim against an employee if the employee has failed to give notice in writing of any claim or proceeding to the board within 30 days after the employee has notice of a claim or if the employee has failed to give such notice within five days after service of a proceeding.
2031:
(a) Where defense of a claim or proceeding against an employee is provided by this division, all final judgments awarded in courts of competent jurisdiction against employees in proceedings to which this division applies or any amount payable under any settlement of such proceeding or of claims in accordance with this division shall be paid by Macon-Bibb County as hereafter provided. All compromises of claims or proceedings governed by this article shall be submitted to the commission for its prior approval.
(b) Notwithstanding the forgoing, payment of judgments and claims shall be limited as follows:
(1) No sum will be paid where the employee's alleged liability is based on a discretionary act or omission. Payment of judgments and claims pursuant to this section shall be made only where liability is based upon a ministerial act of the employee. It is the intent of this section to provide for the payment of claims or judgments only where the defense of sovereign or governmental immunity is not available as a defense to the claim or proceeding. There is, however, excluded from this section payment of any claim against Macon-Bibb County for money for a loss caused by negligence of a Macon-Bibb County officer or employee using a vehicle owned, leased or rented by the county while carrying out his or her official duties or employment pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 36-92-1 et seq.
(2) No sum will be paid on behalf of any employee in excess of $50,000.00 for any one claimant, regardless of the number of claims that claimant may have arising from any one occurrence. In the event of multiple claimants as a result of one occurrence, no sum will be paid in excess of $100,000.00, regardless of the number of claimants or claims. Derivative claims, such as claims for loss of consortium or services, shall not be considered separate claims.
(3) No sum will be paid for punitive or exemplary damages.
(4) No sum will be paid unless the claimant unconditionally releases the employee and Macon-Bibb County from any and all claims, causes of action or judgments arising out of the subject claim or proceeding.
(5) No sum will be paid if Macon-Bibb County has reserved the right not to pay a claim or judgment notwithstanding the acceptance of the defense and if Macon-Bibb County later determines that the claim or proceeding meets one or more of the grounds for refusal of defense enumerated in this section. If Macon-Bibb County reserves the right not to pay a claim or judgment, Macon-Bibb County shall give the employee written notice that Macon-Bibb County has accepted the defense under a reservation of rights.
(6) Notwithstanding the forgoing, the commission may, in its discretion, indemnify an employee for a claim or judgment in excess of $50,000.00 if the commission determines that the best interests of Macon-Bibb County will be served by such additional indemnification. (a) Terms and Definitions. The terms and definitions provided below are specific to Section 19-17, Public-Private Facilities and Infrastructure Act of 2015. These definitions are not applicable in any other sections of this Chapter.
Comprehensive agreement means the written agreement between the private entity and the local government required pursuant to the PPFIA.
Develop or development means to plan, design, develop, finance, lease, acquire, install, construct, operate, maintain or expand.
Interim agreement means an agreement between a private entity and a responsible public entity that provides for phasing of the development or operation, or both, of a qualifying project. Such phases may include, but are not limited to, design, planning, engineering, environmental analysis and mitigation, financial and revenue analysis, or any other phase of the project that constitutes activity on any part of the qualifying project.
Local Government means any county, municipality, consolidated government, or board of education.
Private entity means any natural person, corporation, general partnership, limited liability company, limited partnership, joint venture, business trust, public benefit corporation, nonprofit entity, or other business entity.
Qualifying Project means any project selected in response to a request for a local government or submitted by a private entity as an unsolicited proposal in accordance with the PPFIA and subsequently reviewed and approved by a local government, within its sole discretion, as meeting a public purpose or public need. A "qualifying project" shall not include and shall have no application to any project involving:
(1) The generation of electric energy for sale pursuant to O.C.G.A. tit. 46, ch. 3;
(2) Communications services pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 46-5-4 and 46-5-7;
(3) Cable and video services pursuant to O.C.G.A. tit. 36, ch. 76; or
(4) Water reservoir projects as defined in O.C.G.A. § 12-5-471(10), which shall be governed by O.C.G.A. § 36-91-4.
Revenue means all revenues, income, earnings, user fees, lease payments, or other service payments arising out of or in connection with supporting the development or operation of a qualifying project.
State means the State of Georgia.
Unsolicited Proposal means a written proposal for a qualifying project that is received by a local government and is not in response to any request for proposal for a qualifying project issued by a local government.
(b) Guidelines. The Public-Private Facilities and Infrastructure Act of 2015 (the "PPFIA") (O.C.G.A. § 36-91-110 et seq.) provides a process for local governments to partner with private entities for the development of a wide range of projects for public use if the public entities determine there is a need for such projects and that private involvement may provide such projects to the public in a timely or cost-effective fashion.
In order for a project to come under the PPFIA, it must meet the definition of a "qualifying project." A "qualifying project" is defined broadly under the PPFIA. Specifically, the PPFIA defines a "qualifying project" as any project selected in response to a request for a local government or submitted by a private entity as an unsolicited proposal in accordance with the PPFIA and subsequently reviewed and approved by a local government, within its sole discretion, as meeting a public purpose or public need; provided, however, qualifying projects do not include projects involving generation of electric energy for sale, communications services, cable and video services and water reservoir projects.
The following guidelines have been adopted by the governing body of Macon-Bibb to govern the process for receiving, reviewing and approving unsolicited proposals for qualifying projects.
In the event of any conflict between these guidelines and the PPFIA, the terms of the PPFIA shall control.
(1) Time Period for Receiving Unsolicited Proposals and Format for Submissions.
a. Time Period. Unsolicited proposals for qualifying projects may be received by the Local Government during each year beginning on July 1st and ending on April 1st of the subsequent year (ex. beginning July 1, 2017 through April 1, 2018). Such unsolicited proposals shall be in writing and shall be delivered to the Macon-Bibb County Procurement Department, 700 Poplar Street, Macon, Georgia 31201. Should a proposer have any questions, please contact the procurement director at (478) 803-0550 or email at: procurement@maconbibb.us.
b. Format for Submissions. Unsolicited proposals shall contain, at a minimum, the following information: (a) a project description, (b) a project feasibility statement, (c) a proposed project schedule, (d) a project financing plan, (e) a business case statement that shall include a basic description of any direct and indirect benefits that the private entity can provide in delivering the project, including relevant cost, quality, methodology, and process for identifying the project and time frame data, (f) a description of any anticipated public support or opposition, (g) qualifications and experience, (h) names and addresses of persons who may be contact, and (i) any additional information as the local government may reasonably request to comply with the requirements of the PPFIA. Proposals should be prepared simply and economically, providing a concise description of the proposer's capabilities to complete the proposed qualifying project and the benefits to be derived from the project by the local government. Such proposals may also include any additional pertinent information as determined by the proposer.
Only proposals complying with the requirements of these guidelines and the PPFIA that contain sufficient information for a meaningful evaluation and that are provided in an appropriate format should be considered by the Local Government for further review. If any information necessary to make a meaningful evaluation is missing, the local government may request such information from the proposer. Unsolicited proposals are subject to the Open Records Act.
The format and information to be included in any unsolicited proposal are as follows:
1. Project Description:
(i) Provide a description of the project, including the location of the project, the conceptual design of such facility, or facilities, and a conceptual plan for the provision of services or technological infrastructure.
(ii) Identify and fully describe the scope of work to be performed by the proposer with enough detail to allow an analysis by the local government.
(iii) Identify and fully describe any work to be performed by the local government.
(iv) Identify any anticipated adverse social, economic, and environmental impacts of the project.
(v) Identify the projected positive social, economic, and environmental impacts of the project.
(vi) State assumptions, related to ownership, legal liability, law enforcement, and operation of the project and the existence of any restrictions on the local government's use of the project.
2. Project Feasibility Statement:
(i) A feasibility statement that includes:
(A) The method by which the private entity proposes to secure any necessary property interests required for the project;
(B) A list of all permits and approvals required for the project from local, state, or federal agencies; and
(C) A list of public utility facilities, if any, that will be crossed by the project and a statement of the plans of the private entity to accommodate such crossings.
(ii) Provide a list of any contingencies that must occur for the project to be successful.
(iii) Provide a list of any other assumptions relied on for the project to be successful.
(iv) Provide information relative to ongoing maintenance and operational costs after the project is completed.
3. Project Schedule:
(i) A schedule for initiation, construction, and completion of the project to include the proposed major responsibilities and timeline for activities to be performed by both the local government and private entity.
(ii) A schedule for obtaining all federal, state, and local permits and approvals required for the project.
(iii) Identify the proposed schedule for strategies or actions to mitigate known impacts of the project.
(iv) Provide information relative to phased or partial openings of the proposed project prior to completion of the entire work if applicable.
4. Project Financing Plan:
(i) A financial plan setting forth the private entity's general plans for financing the project, including the sources of the private entity's funds and identification of any dedicated revenue source or proposed debt or equity investment on behalf of the private entity; and description of user fees, lease payments and other service payments over the term of the proposed comprehensive agreement (as defined in the PPFIA); and a methodology and circumstances for changes to such user fees, lease payments and other service payments over time.
(ii) Provide a preliminary estimate and estimating methodology of the cost of the work by phase, segment, or both.
(iii) Submit a plan for the development, financing, and operation of the project showing the anticipated schedule on which funds will be required containing enough detail to allow an analysis by the local government of the financial feasibility of the proposed project. Describe the anticipated costs of and proposed sources and uses for such funds including any anticipated debt service costs. The operational plan should include appropriate staffing levels and associated costs. Include supporting due diligence studies, analyses, or reports. Identify the sources of the private entity's funds and identification of any dedicated revenue source or proposed debt or equity investment on behalf of the private entity.
(iv) Provide a list and discussion of assumptions underlying all major elements of the plan. Assumptions should include all significant fees associated with financing given the recommended financing approach. In addition, complete disclosure of interest rate assumptions should be included. Any ongoing operational fees, if applicable, should also be disclosed as well as any assumptions with regard to increases in such fees.
(v) Identify any local, state, or federal resources that the proposer contemplates requesting for the project. Describe the total commitment, if any, expected from governmental sources and the timing of any anticipated commitment. Such disclosure should include any direct or indirect guarantees or pledges of the local government's credit or revenue.
(vi) Identify the amounts and the terms and conditions for any revenue sources.
(vii) Describe a proposed allocation of risk and liability for work completed beyond the agreement's completion date, and assurances for timely completion of the project.
(viii) Identify any aspect of the project that could disqualify the project from obtaining tax-exempt financing.
The unsolicited proposal may include financing options, including the imposition of user fees, lease payments or other service payments. Such financing arrangements may include the issuance of debt instruments, equity or other securities or obligations. Depending on the local government's authority and the circumstances of each transaction, financing options might also include the use of special purpose entities, sale and lease back transactions, enhanced use leasing, development agreements, conduit financing and other methods allowed by law. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the local government shall not loan money to a private entity in order to finance all or a portion of the qualifying project.
5. Business Case Statement:
(i) A business case statement that shall include a basic description of any direct or indirect benefits that the private entity can provide in delivering the project, including relevant cost, quality, methodology, and process for identifying the project and time frame data.
(ii) Identify who will benefit from the project, how they will benefit, and how the project will benefit the overall community, region, or state. Project benefits to be considered are those occurring during the construction, renovation, expansion or improvement phase and during the life cycle of the project.
(iii) Identify any anticipated public support or opposition, as well as any anticipated government support or opposition, for the project.
(iv) Explain the strategy and plans that will be carried out to involve and inform the general public, business community, and governmental agencies in areas affected by the project.
(v) Specify the strategies or actions to mitigate known impacts of the project.
(vi) Describe the anticipated significant benefits to the community, region or state, including anticipated benefits to the economic condition of the local government and whether the project is critical to attracting or maintaining competitive industries and businesses to the local government or the surrounding region.
(vii) Describe compatibility with the local comprehensive plan, local infrastructure development plans, the capital improvements budget, or other government spending plan.
(viii) Provide relevant proposer cost, quality, methodology, and process for identifying the project and time frame data.
6. Contacts:
(i) The names and addresses of the persons who may be contacted for further information concerning the unsolicited proposal.
(ii) Identify the legal structure of the firm or consortium of firms making the proposal. Identify the organizational structure for the project, the management approach and how each partner and major subcontractor in the structure fits into the overall team.
(iii) Describe the experience of the firm or consortium of firms making the proposal and the key principals involved in the proposed project including experience with projects of comparable size and complexity. Describe the length of time in business, business experience, public sector experience and other engagements of the firm or consortium of firms. Include the identity of any firms that will provide design, construction and completion guarantees and warranties, and a description of such guarantees and warranties.
(iv) Provide the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of persons within the firm or consortium of firms who may be contacted for further information.
(v) Provide a current or most recently audited financial statement of the firm or firms and each partner with an equity interest of twenty percent or greater for project proposals over $20 million dollars.
(vi) Identify any persons known to the proposer who would be obligated to disqualify themselves from participation in any transaction arising from or in connection to the project pursuant to any State of Georgia conflict of interest laws.
(2) Procedures for the Financial Review and Analysis of an Unsolicited Proposal.
a. Upon receipt of an unsolicited proposal, the Local Government shall:
1. Send the proposer an acknowledgement of receipt of the unsolicited proposal and provide that the Local Government will conduct a review of that proposal and either: (a) reject the unsolicited proposal; or (b) accept the unsolicited proposal and seek competing bids for the proposed project as required pursuant to the Guidelines and the PPFIA;
2. Establish a new committee or select an existing committee (the "Evaluation Committee") to review the unsolicited proposal. If a new committee is established, it should be composed of no less than three individuals with diverse skill sets to adequately review the proposal;
3. Decide whether it will engage independent advisors, as provided in subsection (b)(3) below, to assist (and not be a member of) the Evaluation Committee in its review of the unsolicited proposal, which may include an attorney, financial advisor, architectural and/or engineering consultant or other advisers or consultants; and
4. Provide the proposer with the proposed Local Government fee to cover the costs of processing, reviewing and evaluating the unsolicited proposal, as calculated in subsection (b)(4) below.
b. The Evaluation Committee, together with any independent advisors, shall perform the following financial review and analysis of the unsolicited proposal:
1. A cost-benefit analysis;
2. Evaluation of the public need for or benefit derived from the qualifying project;
3. Evaluation of the estimated cost of the qualifying project for reasonableness in relation to similar facilities;
4. Evaluation of the source of funding for the project;
5. Consideration of plans to ensure timely development or operation;
6. Evaluation of risk sharing, including cost or completion guarantees, added value, or debt or equity investments by the private entity; and
7. Consideration of any increase in funding, dedicated revenue source, or other economic benefit that would not otherwise be available.
After reviewing the proposal, the Evaluation Committee shall make a recommendation to the governing body of the Local Government to reject or accept the unsolicited proposal.
(3) Criteria for Identifying and Appointing Independent Advisors. Unsolicited proposals which have technical, complex or specialized information may require additional support from one or more third-party independent advisors to assist in their evaluation and review. Independent advisors may include attorneys, financial advisors, engineering consultants or other advisers or consultants as determined by the Local Government, in its sole discretion, to be reasonably required to review any unsolicited proposal. Independent advisors shall have no affiliation with the private entity submitting an unsolicited proposal.
(4) Criteria for Determining Fees.
a. A private entity assumes all risk in submission of an unsolicited proposal, and a Local Government shall not incur any obligation to reimburse a private entity for any costs, damages, or loss of intellectual property incurred by a private entity in the creation, development, or submission of a proposal or unsolicited proposal for a qualifying project.
b. The Local Government shall charge and retain an initial proposal processing fee equal to $100 to be paid by the proposer prior to the review of an unsolicited proposal.
c. In addition, the Local Government may charge and retain a reasonable fee to cover the costs of reviewing and evaluating an unsolicited proposal. If it is determined by the Local Government that one or more independent advisors shall be engaged to assist the Evaluation Committee in its review of the unsolicited proposal, as provided above, the fees of all such independent advisors shall be paid by the proposer. The estimated fees of the Local Government and such independent advisors shall be provided to the proposer for approval prior to the engagement of such advisors to review the proposal or the review and evaluation of an unsolicited proposal.
(5) Procedures for Determining Release of Information in Unsolicited Proposal. The Local Government, in its sole discretion, may use any portion of an unsolicited proposal in preparing a request for proposal as described in subsection (b)(6) below.
(6) Request for Proposals.
a. Within 60 days of receipt of a recommendation from the Evaluation Committee as provided in subsection (b)(2) above, the governing board of the Local Government shall decide whether to approve or reject such unsolicited proposal. If the local government approves the unsolicited proposal, it shall seek competing proposals for the qualifying project, at the cost of the Local Government, by issuing a request for proposal for not less than 90 days.
b. The request for proposal shall include the criteria for selecting among competing proposals as provided in subsection (b)(8) below.
c. During evaluation, the Local Government may seek written clarification from any proposer regarding the contents of the proposer's response. A request for written clarification may be made when a proposer's response contains conflicting information or is so ambiguous that it is possible for a reasonable person to attribute different meanings to the ambiguous portion of the proposer's response. A request for written clarification may not be used to negotiate (i.e., request the supplier to revise or improve the proposer's response). Written clarifications received from the supplier will become part of that proposer's response.
(7) Procedures for Posting and Publishing Notice of the Opportunity to Offer Competing Proposals.
a. Notices for requests for proposals for qualifying projects shall be posted by the Local Government in a consistent manner with other notices posted for public works bidding as provided by O.C.G.A. § 36-91-1 et seq.
b. Notices for requests for proposals that are advertised in the legal organ shall be advertised a minimum of two times, with the first advertisement occurring at least ninety days prior to the deadline for receipt of competing proposals. The second advertisement shall follow no earlier than six weeks from the first advertisement.
c. Notices for requests for proposals that are advertised solely on the Internet shall be posted continuously at least ninety days prior to the deadline for receipt of competing proposals. Inadvertent or unintentional loss of Internet service during the advertisement period shall not require the contract award or bid or proposal opening to be delayed.
(8) Procedures for Processing, Review and Consideration of Competing Proposals. After the deadline for the receipt of competing proposals, the Local Government shall reconvene the evaluation committee to review, evaluate and score the responses.
The criteria to be used in the evaluation of competing proposals for a qualifying project shall be determined by the evaluation committee of the Local Government prior to submitting a request for proposal for such qualifying project. The evaluation committee of the Local Government shall establish a scoring matrix for review of responses to a request for proposal. The scoring matrix can be weighted in any fair manner to adequately assess the critical elements of a proposal, with the most likely highest weighted categories being: (a) project financing; and (b) qualifications and experience.
There are several factors that the Local Government may use when evaluating and selecting an unsolicited proposal, including, but not limited to, the following:
a. Qualifications and Experience. Factors to be considered to determine whether the proposer possesses the requisite qualifications and experience include:
1. Experience with similar projects;
2. Demonstration of ability to perform work;
3. Leadership structure;
4. Project manager's experience;
5. Management approach;
6. Financial condition; and
7. Project ownership.
b. Project Characteristics. Factors to be considered in determining the project characteristics include:
1. Project definition;
2. Proposed project schedule;
3. Operation of the project;
4. Technology; technical feasibility;
5. Conformity to laws, regulations, and standards;
6. Environmental impacts;
7. Condemnation impacts;
8. State and local permits; and
9. Maintenance of the project.
c. Project Financing. Factors to be considered in determining whether the proposed project financing allows adequate access to the necessary capital to finance the project include:
1. Cost and cost benefit to the local government;
2. Financing and the impact on the debt burden of the local government or appropriating body;
3. Financial plan, including the degree to which the proposer has conducted due diligence investigation and analysis of the proposed financial plan and the results of any such inquiries or studies;
4. Opportunity costs assessment;
5. Estimated cost;

(a) Determination of noncompliance or refusal to precertify. The contract compliance hearing officer shall cause notice of the hearing to be served upon all parties, by registered mail. Such notice shall set forth with particularity the charges filed by the aggrieved party and shall include the hearing date, time and place.
